annotationRationale: The equation reduces to zero together with the sixth roots of unity. Both methods use modulus; the first counts roots algebraically, while the second uses polar angles and complex powers.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate for this complex equation.

review.questionCheck: Taking moduli gives |z|=0 or 1. The nonzero solutions are exactly the six sixth roots of unity, so there are seven solutions, agreeing with choice E and the key. No figures or mathematical contradictions are present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The algebraic and polar routes are both retained and independently complete. LIVE and AoPS Solutions 1 and 4 are incorporated into the modulus reduction; AoPS Solution 2 supplies the polar route. AoPS Solution 3 does not provide a sound additional count because its right-hand side a²+b² depends on the unknown. No shared-bank methods were supplied, and no further route is needed.
review.annotationCheck: Roots of unity correctly describe the assessed nonzero solution set, with modulus as support. Method-specific conjugate-product, quadratic-solution, and polar-power concepts are accurately recorded.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is appropriate for this complex equation.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The nonnegative modulus equation has precisely the cases 0 and 1. The displayed factorization of z⁶-1 is correct and yields six distinct unit-modulus roots. The converse z⁵=1/z=conjugate(z) verifies that no extraneous roots were introduced. Including zero gives seven.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The claimed LIVE and AoPS Solutions 1 and 4 basis is accurate. The explicit factorization, quadratic roots, and converse check extend the source reasoning in original explanatory prose. Both third-party references are credited appropriately.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The modulus comparison is motivated, zero is handled before division, and the six-root count is established explicitly rather than assumed from an unexplained theorem.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Geometric modulus, the conjugate product within cnm_h104, roots of unity, and complex solutions of real quadratics all appear directly. cnm_h104 is used within its limited supplied scope.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native geometric-complex and simple-power/conjugate-product links support the modulus reduction. No accepted CN links are supplied for roots of unity or the complex-quadratic node.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: N-CN.C.7 directly fits solving the two real-coefficient quadratics. The narrower N-CN.B.4 and N-CN.A.3 links provide rectangular-plane and conjugate/modulus connections only. The partial N-CN.B.6 distance/midpoint link is not exercised as a full task; roots of unity have no accepted US link.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All four direct IDs match their definitions and the derivation. The root-counting concept is supported by a complete elementary calculation.

methodReviews.mathCheck: For nonzero z, r⁵=r forces r=1. Equality of arguments gives 6θ=2πk. The half-open interval 0≤θ<2π selects exactly k=0 through 5, without duplicating an endpoint. These six values satisfy the equation, and zero adds the seventh.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solution 2 genuinely supplies the polar approach. The candidate uses original prose and simplifies the radial argument correctly by requiring r>0. It makes no official-source claim.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation states the multiplication and conjugation angle rules at use, explains whole-turn ambiguity, and explicitly counts the permitted argument classes.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Modulus, polar powers, and cyclic complex-root counting are all justified. The precise polar node avoids treating elementary powers of i as sufficient coverage.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The supplied exact geometric-complex link supports modulus and the complex-plane setting. There are no accepted CN links for the polar-power or roots-of-unity nodes.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The narrower N-CN.B.4 and N-CN.B.5 links genuinely support polar representation, multiplication, and geometric conjugation here, without covering all listed operations. N-CN.A.3 supplies a conjugate/modulus connection; N-CN.B.6 midpoint coverage is absent. Roots of unity remain an accepted-link gap.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The three direct IDs precisely match the modulus restriction and angle-class count, with the nonzero domain and endpoint convention explicit.
